note: Addresses the common client case of using pretrained or off the shelf models, and ties actions to ISO 27090 and OWASP.
title: Compliance Made Practical: Translating the EU AI Act into Implementable Security Actions
journal: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Responsible AI Engineering
explain_beginner: New AI regulations in Europe require companies to make their AI systems secure, but it's unclear what concrete steps they should take. This paper explains how companies using existing AI models can follow these rules by connecting regulatory requirements to practical security actions. It bridges the gap between official guidelines and real-world implementation, helping organizations understand their responsibilities and what they must do to protect their systems.
explain_business: Organizations deploying commercial or pretrained AI models now face regulatory compliance obligations under EU AI Act and emerging ISO 27090 standards, but lack clear implementation roadmaps. This work translates regulatory requirements into specific, achievable security actions your teams can execute. It enables informed decisions about risk mitigation investments, clarifies compliance responsibilities, and provides a framework for demonstrating due diligence to regulators and stakeholders.
explain_practitioner: This work synthesizes the EU AI Act's security mandates with ISO/IEC standards and OWASP frameworks to create actionable implementation guidance. The paper maps regulatory requirements onto practical security strategies, specifically addressing the common scenario of deploying pretrained or commercial models. It provides concrete mitigation approaches tied to ISO 27090 and OWASP standards, clarifying responsibility allocation and sufficient compliance measures for practitioners building AI systems with existing components.
